title: Gastric / Esophageal Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. ONCOTREE navigator for upper gastrointestinal carcinoma: it captures the physician-entered histology (esophageal squamous vs adenocarcinoma of esophagus/GEJ/stomach), workup, clinical stage/setting, and the biomarkers that steer therapy (HER2, PD-L1 CPS, MMR/MSI, Claudin18.2), then routes to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference. Adenocarcinoma of the distal esophagus, GEJ, and stomach share one metastatic biomarker-directed subtree. The navigator invents no dose, regimen, or eligibility criterion; where no existing protocol fits a leaf, the regimen is described in bullets only. Structural taxonomy consistent with standard guidelines (NCCN Esophageal and Esophagogastric Junction / Gastric Cancer); no proprietary content reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard guidelines (NCCN Gastric / Esophageal), DeVita, and Harrison. Treatment options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers.

a.text: Perioperative FLOT (4 cycles before and 4 after surgery) is preferred over older platinum-fluoropyrimidine triplets for fit patients with resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; benefit is greatest with an R0 D2 resection.

b.text: Neoadjuvant chemoradiation on the CROSS backbone (weekly carboplatin plus paclitaxel with 41.4 Gy) followed by surgery improves R0 rate and survival for locally advanced resectable esophageal/GEJ cancer of either histology.

c.text: Adjuvant nivolumab for up to 1 year is offered when residual pathologic disease (non-pCR) remains after neoadjuvant chemoradiation and R0 resection (CheckMate 577 population).

d.text: First-line metastatic therapy is layered on biomarkers: add anti-PD-1 for PD-L1 CPS-positive tumors, trastuzumab for HER2-positive, zolbetuximab for Claudin18.2-positive, and favor immunotherapy for MMR-deficient/MSI-high disease. Test all four up front.

bullets.sub: document tumor length and distance from incisors

bullets.label: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)
bullets.sub: cT/cN depth when not overtly metastatic

bullets: CT chest/abdomen with contrast

nodes.name: SCC stage
nodes.title: Esophageal SCC: clinical stage / setting
nodes.description: Physician-entered clinical stage. ONCOTREE does not compute stage; enter the confirmed cTNM-based setting.

tables.title: SCC clinical stage buckets (simplified)
rows: Neoadjuvant chemoRT then surgery, or definitive chemoRT

nodes.name: SCC early
nodes.title: Early SCC: endoscopic or surgical resection
nodes.description: T1a is usually cured by endoscopic resection (EMR/ESD); T1b or unfavorable histology may need esophagectomy. No systemic protocol is expected here.
bullets: EMR/ESD for T1a with favorable pathology
Esophagectomy for T1b or deep/lymphovascular involvement
Surveillance endoscopy after endoscopic resection

nodes.name: SCC locally advanced
nodes.title: Locally advanced SCC: surgical vs definitive approach
nodes.description: Fit surgical candidates receive neoadjuvant chemoradiation then esophagectomy; non-surgical patients (proximal tumors, comorbidity, patient choice) receive definitive chemoradiation.

nodes.name: SCC neoadjuvant chemoRT
nodes.title: Locally advanced SCC: neoadjuvant chemoRT (CROSS) then surgery
nodes.description: Weekly carboplatin plus paclitaxel with concurrent radiotherapy, then esophagectomy. Adjuvant nivolumab is offered for residual pathologic disease after R0 resection.

nodes.name: SCC definitive chemoRT
nodes.title: Locally advanced SCC: definitive chemoradiation
nodes.description: Concurrent chemoradiation without planned surgery, favored for cervical/proximal tumors or non-surgical patients. No existing protocol matches this regimen; described here for reference.

bullets.label: Cisplatin + fluorouracil (or carboplatin/paclitaxel) with concurrent RT

bullets: Salvage esophagectomy for local persistence/recurrence in fit patients
Response assessed by endoscopy/biopsy and PET/CT

nodes.name: SCC metastatic PD-L1
nodes.title: Metastatic SCC: PD-L1 CPS status
nodes.description: First-line metastatic esophageal SCC adds an anti-PD-1 antibody to chemotherapy when PD-L1 CPS is positive; low-CPS disease is treated with chemotherapy.

options.label: PD-L1 CPS low / negative or unknown

nodes.name: SCC met chemo + IO
nodes.title: Metastatic SCC, CPS-positive: chemotherapy + anti-PD-1
nodes.description: Fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab or nivolumab (nivolumab + ipilimumab is an alternative). No existing metastatic-SCC immunotherapy protocol is present; regimen described in bullets.
bullets: Cisplatin/oxaliplatin + fluoropyrimidine as the chemotherapy backbone
Add pembrolizumab or nivolumab (anti-PD-1)
Nivolumab + ipilimumab is a chemotherapy-sparing alternative in selected patients

nodes.name: SCC met chemo
nodes.title: Metastatic SCC, CPS low: chemotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum-fluoropyrimidine doublet first-line; taxane or irinotecan-based regimens in later lines. Best supportive care and dysphagia palliation throughout.
bullets: First-line platinum + fluoropyrimidine doublet
Later-line taxane or irinotecan-based therapy
Stent/RT for dysphagia; nutrition support

nodes.name: SCC surveillance
nodes.title: Post-curative surveillance (SCC)
nodes.description: Surveillance after curative-intent therapy aims to catch treatable local recurrence and manage late toxicity; most recurrences are within 2 years.
bullets: CT chest/abdomen and endoscopy as clinically indicated
Nutrition, stricture dilation, and swallowing follow-up
Symptom-directed imaging for suspected recurrence

nodes.name: SCC recurrence
nodes.title: SCC: recurrence check
nodes.description: Route by surveillance outcome. Documented distant recurrence enters the metastatic SCC pathway; isolated local recurrence may still be salvageable.

nodes.name: SCC remission
nodes.title: SCC: continued remission
nodes.description: No evidence of disease. Continue the surveillance schedule and supportive care; no active systemic therapy.
bullets: Continue scheduled surveillance
Ongoing nutrition and symptom support

nodes.title: Esophageal / GEJ adenocarcinoma: workup checklist
nodes.description: Same anatomic staging as SCC plus the full adenocarcinoma biomarker panel, which drives metastatic and later-line therapy.
bullets: Upper endoscopy with biopsy; Siewert classification for GEJ
EUS for cT/cN, CT chest/abdomen, FDG-PET/CT

bullets.label: Biomarker panel on tumor tissue
bullets.sub: HER2 IHC/ISH, PD-L1 CPS, MMR/MSI, Claudin18.2

bullets: Staging laparoscopy with peritoneal cytology for cT3-4 or GEJ Siewert II-III
Nutrition and ECOG assessment

nodes.name: Esophageal/GEJ adeno stage
nodes.title: Esophageal / GEJ adenocarcinoma: clinical stage / setting
nodes.description: Physician-entered clinical stage. Resectable locally advanced disease is the decision point between perioperative chemotherapy and neoadjuvant chemoradiation.

nodes.name: Esophageal/GEJ adeno early
nodes.title: Early esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma: endoscopic or surgical resection
nodes.description: T1a is treated by endoscopic resection (with Barrett ablation as needed); T1b or high-risk features warrant esophagectomy. No systemic protocol is expected here.
bullets: EMR/ESD for T1a plus ablation of residual Barrett metaplasia
Esophagectomy for T1b or unfavorable pathology
Endoscopic surveillance thereafter

nodes.name: Esophageal/GEJ adeno LA approach
nodes.title: Locally advanced esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma: perioperative vs neoadjuvant chemoRT
nodes.description: Both perioperative FLOT chemotherapy and neoadjuvant CROSS chemoradiation are standard for resectable disease; GEJ tumors are eligible for either.

nodes.name: Esophageal/GEJ adeno FLOT
nodes.title: Locally advanced esophageal/GEJ adeno: perioperative FLOT
nodes.description: Four cycles of FLOT before and four after surgery for fit patients with resectable adenocarcinoma. Physician selects; the dose engine computes doses.

nodes.name: Esophageal/GEJ adeno CROSS
nodes.title: Locally advanced esophageal/GEJ adeno: neoadjuvant chemoRT (CROSS)
nodes.description: Carboplatin plus paclitaxel with concurrent radiotherapy, then esophagectomy; adjuvant nivolumab for residual pathologic disease after R0 resection.

nodes.name: Gastric adeno workup
nodes.title: Gastric adenocarcinoma: workup checklist
nodes.description: Add staging laparoscopy with peritoneal cytology to the standard workup, since occult peritoneal disease changes intent.
bullets: Upper endoscopy with biopsy and tumor mapping
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis; EUS for early lesions

bullets.label: Biomarker panel
bullets.sub: HER2 IHC/ISH, PD-L1 CPS, MMR/MSI, Claudin18.2

bullets: Nutrition, weight loss, and ECOG assessment

nodes.name: Gastric adeno stage
nodes.title: Gastric adenocarcinoma: clinical stage / setting
nodes.description: Physician-entered clinical stage. Resectable disease beyond T1 receives perioperative chemotherapy; metastatic disease enters the shared biomarker-directed pathway.

nodes.name: Gastric adeno early
nodes.title: Early gastric adenocarcinoma: endoscopic or surgical resection
nodes.description: cT1a lesions meeting criteria are cured by EMR/ESD; otherwise gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy. No systemic protocol is expected here.
bullets: EMR/ESD for guideline-fit cT1a lesions
Gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy otherwise
Endoscopic and nutritional surveillance

nodes.name: Gastric adeno resectable
nodes.title: Resectable gastric adeno: perioperative FLOT (or adjuvant CAPOX)
nodes.description: Perioperative FLOT for fit patients is preferred; adjuvant capecitabine-oxaliplatin after upfront D2 resection is an alternative. Physician selects; the dose engine computes doses.

nodes.name: Adeno metastatic HER2
nodes.title: Metastatic adenocarcinoma: HER2 status
nodes.description: Shared first-line pathway for metastatic adenocarcinoma of the esophagus, GEJ, and stomach. HER2 status is the first fork; HER2-positive disease adds trastuzumab-based therapy.

nodes.name: Adeno met HER2+
nodes.title: Metastatic adeno, HER2-positive: chemo + trastuzumab (+/- anti-PD-1)
nodes.description: Fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy plus trastuzumab first-line; pembrolizumab is added for PD-L1 CPS-positive tumors. Trastuzumab deruxtecan is a later-line option. Chemo backbone via protocol; HER2 agents described in bullets.
bullets: Add trastuzumab to the fluoropyrimidine-platinum backbone
Add pembrolizumab when PD-L1 CPS is positive
Trastuzumab deruxtecan in later lines after progression

nodes.name: Adeno met biomarker
nodes.title: Metastatic adeno, HER2-negative: biomarker-directed option
nodes.description: For HER2-negative metastatic adenocarcinoma, select the highest-priority actionable biomarker. Overlaps are common; MSI-high generally takes precedence, then Claudin18.2 and PD-L1 CPS layer onto chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Adeno met MSI-H
nodes.title: Metastatic adeno, MSI-high: anti-PD-1
nodes.description: MMR-deficient/MSI-high metastatic adenocarcinoma is highly immunotherapy-responsive; pembrolizumab (with or without chemotherapy) is preferred first-line.

nodes.name: Adeno met CPS+
nodes.title: Metastatic adeno, CPS-positive: chemo + anti-PD-1
nodes.description: Fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (or nivolumab) for PD-L1 CPS-positive HER2-negative disease.

nodes.name: Adeno met Claudin18.2+
nodes.title: Metastatic adeno, Claudin18.2-positive: chemo + zolbetuximab
nodes.description: Fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin chemotherapy plus zolbetuximab for Claudin18.2-positive, HER2-negative disease. Chemo backbone via protocol; zolbetuximab described in bullets.
bullets: Add zolbetuximab (anti-Claudin18.2) to the fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin backbone
Premedicate for nausea/vomiting, which is dose-limiting early
Reserve anti-PD-1 for co-positive CPS per clinical judgement

nodes.name: Adeno met standard
nodes.title: Metastatic adeno, no actionable biomarker: chemotherapy
nodes.description: Fluoropyrimidine-platinum doublet first-line; ramucirumab-paclitaxel is the preferred second line, then irinotecan-based therapy or trifluridine-tipiracil.
bullets: First-line FOLFOX / CAPOX doublet
Second-line ramucirumab + paclitaxel
Later-line FOLFIRI or trifluridine-tipiracil

nodes.name: Adeno surveillance
nodes.title: Post-curative surveillance (adenocarcinoma)
nodes.description: Surveillance after curative-intent perioperative therapy and resection; watch for recurrence and manage post-gastrectomy nutrition.
bullets: CT and endoscopy as clinically indicated

bullets.label: Nutritional monitoring
bullets.sub: B12, iron, calcium/vitamin D after gastrectomy

bullets: Symptom-directed imaging for suspected recurrence

nodes.name: Adeno recurrence
nodes.title: Adenocarcinoma: recurrence check
nodes.description: Route by surveillance outcome. Documented recurrence re-enters the shared metastatic biomarker-directed pathway (re-biopsy to reconfirm HER2/CPS/MSI/Claudin when feasible).

nodes.name: Adeno remission
nodes.title: Adenocarcinoma: continued remission
nodes.description: No evidence of disease. Continue surveillance and post-gastrectomy nutritional support; no active systemic therapy.
bullets: Continue scheduled surveillance
Ongoing nutritional and symptom support
